fullPassage:
When she woke the next day, the house was silent.
'Perhaps the disease has gone,' she thought, 'and everybody is well again. I wonder who will take care of me instead of Kamala? Why doesn't someone bring me some food? It's strange the house is so quiet.'
But just then she heard men's voices in the hall.
'How sad!' said one. 'That beautiful woman! She died last night.'
'And the husband, too, wasn't he?'
'But is there a child, too, wasn't there?'
'Mary was standing in the middle of her room when they opened the door a few minutes later. The men looked at her in surprise.
'My name is Mary,' she said crossly. 'I was asleep when everyone was ill. And I'm hungry. Why has nobody come to take care of me?'
The younger man stared at her. 'Poor child!' he said. 'You see, there's nobody left alive in the house. So you'll have to come with us to England.'
But Mary did not understand. She only knew her father and mother were dead, and she had nobody to take care of her.
Because she had never known her parents well, she did not miss them at all. She only felt angry.
They arrived at a very old house. It looked dark and unfriendly from the outside. Mary looked around its shadow to a room, where there was a warm fire and food on the table.
'This is where you'll live, Miss Mary,' said Mrs Medlock. 'Go to bed when you're tired. And remember, you must stay in your room! Mr Craven doesn't want you to go walking about the house.'
Martha did not seem to mind Mary's crossness. 'I know. I talk too much!' she laughed. 'Are you going to be my servant?' asked Mary. 'Well, I work for Mrs Medlock. I'm going to clean your room and bring you your food, but you won't need a servant except for those things.' 'But who's going to dress me?' Martha stopped and stared at Mary. 'Tha' canna' dress thyself?' she asked, shocked. 'What do you mean? I don't understand your language!' 'Oh, I forgot. We all speak the Yorkshire dialect here, but of course you don't understand that. I meant to say, can't you put on your own clothes? Of course not! My servant always used to dress me.' 'Well I think you should learn to dress yourself. My mother always says people should be able to take care of themselves, even if they're rich and important.'
Little Miss Mary was furious with Martha. 'It's difficult in India where I come from! You don't know anything about India, or about servants! You ... you ...' She could not explain what she meant. Suddenly she felt very confused and lonely. She threw herself down on the bed and started crying wildly.

det.korean: wild → wildly: 동사 crying을 수식하는 부사 형태
det.analysis: wild(형용사: 거친, 사나운) → wildly(부사: 격하게, 거칠게). 동사 crying 뒤에서 '어떻게 울었는지'를 수식하는 부사 필요. 'started crying wildly'=격하게 울기 시작했다
det.tip: wild(adj.) → wildly(adv.). 동사를 수식할 때 부사형(-ly) 사용

questions.passage:
When she woke the next day, the house was silent.
'Perhaps the disease has gone,' she thought, 'and everybody is well again. I wonder who will take care of me instead of Kamala? Why doesn't someone bring me some food? It's strange the house is so quiet.'
But just then she heard men's voices in the hall.
'How sad!' said one. 'That beautiful woman! She died last night.'
'And the husband, too, wasn't he?'
'But is there a child, too, wasn't there?'
'Mary was standing in the middle of her room when they opened the door a few minutes later. The men looked at her in surprise.
'My name is Mary,' she said crossly. 'I was asleep when everyone was ill. And I'm hungry. Why has nobody come to take care of me?'
The younger man stared at her. 'Poor child!' he said. 'You see, there's nobody left alive in the house. So you'll have to come with us to England.'
But Mary did not understand. She only knew her father and mother were dead, and she had nobody to take care of her.
Because she had never known her parents well, she did not miss them at all. She only felt angry.
They arrived at a very old house. It looked dark and unfriendly from the outside. Mary looked around its shadow to a room, where there was a warm fire and food on the table.
'This is where you'll live, Miss Mary,' said Mrs Medlock. 'Go to bed when you're tired. And remember, you must stay in your room! Mr Craven doesn't want you to go __________the house.'
Martha did not seem to mind Mary's crossness. 'I know. I talk too much!' she laughed. 'Are you going to be my servant?' asked Mary. 'Well, I work for Mrs Medlock. I'm going to clean your room and bring you your food, but you won't need a servant except for those things.' 'But who's going to dress me?' Martha stopped and stared at Mary. 'Tha' canna' dress thyself?' she asked, shocked. 'What do you mean? I don't understand your language!' 'Oh, I forgot. We all speak the Yorkshire dialect here, but of course you don't understand that. I meant to say, can't you put on your own clothes? Of course not! My servant always used to dress me.' 'Well I think you should learn to dress yourself. My mother always says people should be able to take care of themselves, even if they're rich and important.'
Little Miss Mary was furious with Martha. 'It's difficult in India where I come from! You don't know anything about India, or about servants! You ... you ...' She could not explain what she meant. Suddenly she felt very confused and lonely. She threw herself down on the bed and started crying wildly.

det.korean: Mr Craven은 Mary가 집 안을 __________ 것을 원하지 않았다
det.analysis:
❌ ① running around(뛰어다니는): 원문은 '돌아다니는'이지 뛰는 것이 아님
✅ ② walking about(돌아다니는): 집 안을 돌아다니지 말라는 지시 ← 정답
❌ ③ cleaning up(청소하는): 청소 금지가 아닌 돌아다님 금지
❌ ④ looking into(들여다보는): 집을 조사하는 것이 아님
det.tip: walk about=돌아다니다(syn: wander around). Mr Craven이 Mary의 행동을 제한하는 맥락

overlay.blank: she did not miss them at all

det.korean: 부모를 잘 몰랐기 때문에 __________
det.analysis:
❌ ① she cried for them every night(매일 밤 울었다): 부모를 잘 몰라서 울지 않았음
❌ ② she wanted to find them again(다시 찾고 싶었다): 이미 죽었다는 것을 알고 있었고 그리워하지 않음
❌ ③ she remembered them fondly(다정하게 기억했다): 잘 모르는 부모를 다정하게 기억할 수 없음
✅ ④ she did not miss them at all(전혀 그리워하지 않았다): 부모를 잘 몰랐기에 그리워하지 않음 ← 정답
det.tip: miss=그리워하다. 'not ~ at all'=전혀 ~않다. Mary의 냉담함과 고립된 성장 배경
